newsitem.title: BRAZIL: High Brazil fx reserves could spur rate ease - paper.
newsitem.headline: High Brazil fx reserves could spur rate ease - paper.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan sees no reasons for Brazil to keep accumulating foreign reserves, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said on Friday.

With a high level of reserves, the government feels more comfortable reducing domestic interest rates since the country no longer needs to make them attractive enough to foreign investors, Gazeta said.
The foreign reserves, which currently total $59.6 billion, were accumulated to be used according to the country's interests, Malan told the newspaper in an interview.
"If it is necessary to use them, we have a comfortable enough level (of reserves) to allow a margin of fluctuation," he was quoted as saying.
Malan told Gazeta there is a trend for a gradual reduction in interest rates.
"But how gradual it will be, we will not announce," he was quoted as saying.
According to the newspaper, Malan also said investors should pay attention to the performance of the futures markets, which have been projecting low inflation rates.
